executive_summary.portal_profile: SMP Security operates a HubSpot Standard portal with 2,661 contacts, 632 companies, 1,268 deals, and 2 tickets. The portal has been in active use for several years and continues to see active development.
executive_summary.narrative: Your foundational architecture is strong. Your strategic infrastructure (persona framework, AI scoring, cross-sell segmentation, Target Accounts) is ahead of peer portals. The gap is concentrated in two areas: operational discipline (calling, deal ownership, activity capture) and the CONVERT tier's list-and-workflow infrastructure.

top_risks.title: Single-owner pipeline concentration
top_risks.detail: 99 of 100 open deals are owned by one user. Business continuity risk on $667K+ of tracked pipeline.

top_risks.title: Activity capture blind spot
top_risks.detail: One logged call in 30 days across 11 owners. Calls happen off-platform; coaching and pipeline analysis impossible.

top_risks.title: CONVERT tier execution gap
top_risks.detail: 11 of 17 required CONVERT lists missing. No stalled deal alert workflow. No lead reassignment automation. No MQL-to-SQL handoff. This is where warm opportunities currently die.

top_opportunities.title: Activate the 27 sequences already built
top_opportunities.detail: Your portal has 27 sequences in place. None currently have enrollments. The infrastructure is waiting for the operational discipline to use it.

top_opportunities.title: Deploy CONVERT-tier lists and workflows
top_opportunities.detail: Populating the 11 missing CONVERT lists and the four missing workflows produces immediate pipeline visibility. This is Quantum's Q2 core package territory.

top_opportunities.title: Bring calls into the platform
top_opportunities.detail: Call capture closes the single largest data gap in the portal. Once active, AI scoring (which you already have) becomes predictive instead of descriptive.

executive_summary.next_step: A targeted cleanup engagement, not a rebuild. Week 1 focuses on quick wins that resolve the critical findings. Month 1 tackles the strategic enablers. Quarter 1 scopes the larger investments. Total early-engagement scope: roughly 80 to 100 hours.

maturity.overall_narrative: Limited by Technology & Integration Coverage and People & Adoption. Your strategic infrastructure is built to support a higher operational stage than your current discipline layer can execute.

stages.observation: Pipeline stages well-designed; deal progression discipline gaps and no documented buying centers.
Property governance visible, lists well-structured, naming conventions used.

data_health.title: 1.1 Deal amount missing on 77 of 100 open deals
data_health.evidence: Of 100 open deals, only 23 have a populated amount field.
data_health.impact: Pipeline forecasting cannot function without deal amounts. Revenue planning, capacity modeling, and resource allocation all depend on a pipeline that shows expected value.
data_health.recommendation: Enforce amount as required at Site Visited/Needs Assessment stage via blocking workflow. Backfill existing open deals through owner assessment session.

data_health.title: 1.2 No buying roles identified on any open deal
data_health.evidence: All 100 open deals examined: zero Decision Makers, 87 single-threaded with one associated contact.
data_health.impact: Buying role documentation is the foundation of modern B2B forecast accuracy.
data_health.recommendation: Add buying role fields to Deal record sidebar. Require Decision Maker before Proposal Sent stage. Build weekly review for deals missing roles.

data_health.title: 1.3 Historical deal ownership on deactivated or unknown user
data_health.evidence: Owner ID 62088901 not in active owners list, associated with 464 historical deals — 37% of total deals ever created.
data_health.impact: Historical deal reporting, rep-level analysis, and any ownership-over-time analytics include orphaned/misattributed records.
data_health.recommendation: Identify the phantom owner. Bulk-reassign to Archive owner.

data_health.title: 1.4 Phone number populated on only 27% of contacts
data_health.impact: Security services business with phone as primary channel; outbound motion cannot operate against majority of database.
data_health.recommendation: Deploy enrichment service (ZoomInfo, Apollo). Enforce capture on new contacts via workflow.

data_health.title: 1.5 Job title populated on only 24% of contacts
data_health.evidence: Sample: 24% job title fill. Persona trigger lists (C-Suite, Facilities, HR/Safety, IT, Ops) require job title.
data_health.impact: Persona framework cannot operate on 76% of contacts.
data_health.recommendation: Enrich in parallel with phone. Enforce on form submissions.

data_health.title: 1.6 Close-lost reason captured on only 51% of lost deals
data_health.evidence: 61 closed-lost deals in 365d; 31 have closed_lost_reason populated.
data_health.impact: Win-loss analysis operates on less than half available signal. 72% win rate means understanding the other 28% is a competitive intelligence gap.
data_health.recommendation: Make closed_lost_reason required on stage change to Closed Lost. Backfill recent losses. Quarterly win-loss review.

architecture.title: 2.1 Consider custom objects for Systems and Monitoring Contracts
architecture.evidence: Portal has no custom objects. Two industry-standard candidates for security integration businesses: Installed Systems and Monitoring Contracts.
architecture.impact: Without these, equipment lifecycles not visible in CRM; monitoring contract renewals cannot be automated; recurring revenue compounded onto Deal rather than separately tracked.
architecture.recommendation: Scope custom object architecture engagement with Company associations, lifecycle fields, renewal tracking. Unlocks the renewal motion your contract-ending lists already anticipate.

adoption.title: 3.1 Pipeline ownership concentrated on a single user
adoption.evidence: 99 of 100 open deals owned by one user. Two other SMP owners own zero open deals.
adoption.impact: Operational continuity at risk on $667K+ tracked pipeline. Coaching and rep-level comparison impossible.
adoption.recommendation: Deal coverage/reassignment policy discussion. Evaluate territory or industry segmentation.

adoption.title: 3.2 Severe call logging gap
adoption.evidence: 1 call logged in 30d across 11 owners. Against 95 emails and 100+ meetings.
adoption.impact: Calls happening off-platform; coaching impossible; pipeline analysis unreliable.
adoption.recommendation: Deploy call capture. HubSpot Calling (fastest) or third-party dialer with auto-log.

adoption.title: 3.3 Five of eleven owner seats show zero activity
adoption.evidence: Inactive seats: Mary Vogel, three Accelant users, one gmail.com account.
adoption.impact: Each category (unused capacity, stale access, passive role) warrants different response.
adoption.recommendation: Audit each seat. Deactivate unused. Migrate gmail to corporate or deactivate.

adoption.title: 3.4 Sequences infrastructure built but unused
adoption.evidence: 27 sequences detected in portal. Zero contacts currently enrolled. Sequences were built but are not in active use.
adoption.impact: Represents significant prior investment (infrastructure and content creation time) producing zero current return. Also a risk: if the sequence content is stale, activating them without review could damage deliverability.
adoption.recommendation: Review sequences for current accuracy. Select 3-5 highest-value sequences to reactivate. Pair with sales rep training on enrollment workflow.
adoption.effort_tier: 4-8 hours sequence review plus 2-4 hours training.

automation.title: 4.1 QuickBooks Online integration workflows recently disabled
automation.evidence: QBO integration workflows turned off April 3, 2026 — three weeks before audit.
automation.impact: If unintentional, revenue-to-invoice flow may be broken.
automation.recommendation: Determine why workflows were disabled. Reactivate or replace.

integrations.title: 5.1 Breeze AI adoption is ahead of peer portals
integrations.evidence: Breeze Prospecting Agent, Chat Assistant, and AI Fit Score / Engagement Score workflows all active.
integrations.impact: Strength to preserve. Most portals at this maturity level have not deployed these.
integrations.recommendation: Continue. Quarterly review to evaluate new Breeze capabilities. Validate Fit Score correlation with win rate.

integrations.title: 5.2 No ad accounts or social channels connected
integrations.evidence: Marketing Hub Pro includes ad/social account connections — none connected.
integrations.impact: Marketing attribution impossible across paid and social. Campaign ROI cannot be measured.
integrations.recommendation: Evaluate paid marketing strategy. If active, connect relevant accounts.

integrations.title: 5.3 No conversation intelligence tool detected
integrations.evidence: No Gong, Chorus, Fireflies, or equivalent CI tool signals detected in workflows or integrations.
integrations.impact: Once call capture is activated (Finding 3.2), CI is the highest-ROI AI investment available for a sales team. Team currently has no recording, coaching, or insight extraction capability.
integrations.recommendation: Evaluate CI options after call capture is stable. Gong is most comprehensive; Fireflies is lightest weight.
integrations.effort_tier: 2-3 weeks deployment; subscription cost varies by team size.

feature_matrix_headlines.sales: Sales Hub headline: Pipeline design (SH-03) is genuinely strong, but 9 of 13 audited features score No or Partial. The standout finding — 27 sequences built with zero current enrollments — indicates the infrastructure is waiting on operational adoption. Activating Calling and Sequences is the single highest-ROI Sales Hub intervention available.
feature_matrix_headlines.marketing: Marketing Hub headline: list architecture and persona segmentation are strong. Marketing emails, landing pages, campaigns, ad accounts, and social channels are all completely unused — the inbound and paid marketing motion is essentially dormant. If inbound is a strategic priority, this is the area with the most unrealized capacity.
feature_matrix_headlines.service: Service Hub is present but dormant (2 tickets). For a security business with recurring customer relationships, tickets, SLAs, and knowledge base are a natural fit that could support renewal conversations and customer self-service. Knowledge base requires Service Pro upgrade.
feature_matrix_headlines.ai_breeze: AI feature adoption is ahead of peer portals. Breeze Prospecting Agent, Chat Assistant, and AI Fit/Engagement scoring are all active, with workflows keying off the scores. This is a strength to preserve and extend. A Predictive Lead Scoring upgrade (Enterprise tier) would extend what is already an ahead-of-peer AI adoption posture.
feature_matrix_headlines.third_party_ai: Detection for third-party AI (Claude, ChatGPT) requires OAuth and installed-apps inspection not available through the standard audit. A brief direct check in HubSpot Settings > Integrations can confirm what is connected.
feature_matrix_headlines.conversation_intel: Conversation intelligence is the single most impactful AI investment for a sales team actively on phones. Given the current call-capture gap, deploying any CI tool (Gong, Chorus, Fireflies) depends on first activating call capture per the Adoption findings.

revefficiency.interpretation: Interpretation: your KEEP, GROW, MULTIPLY, and EXPAND tiers are all functionally ready. The CONVERT tier — typically the largest revenue recovery opportunity in any portal — is where the gap concentrates. This is also where Quantum's Q2 core packages produce the highest marginal value.

tier_observations.KEEP: Retention infrastructure solid. Minor gap: QBR tracking not formalized.
tier_observations.GROW: Cross-sell and upsell segmentation lists present and well-organized.
tier_observations.MULTIPLY: Referral program structure not formalized; LinkedIn integration signals not visible.
tier_observations.CONVERT: Limiting tier. 11 of 17 required CONVERT lists missing; no MQL/SQL handoff workflow; no stalled deal alerts.

KEEP.heading: Retain current clients
KEEP.summary: Score: 89 (Good). Two structural gaps, neither critical.

paragraphs.body: Gaps identified: QBR tracking (−8 High, no properties or lists for quarterly business reviews), dormant customer detection (−3 Medium, no dedicated list for customers with no activity in 90+ days). For a security services business with recurring customer relationships, adding a QBR cadence property and dormant customer list is low-effort and high-visibility.
Gaps identified: Re-sell / expansion tracking (−3 Medium). Cross-sell and upsell lists detected — healthy signal.

Gaps identified: Referral program structure (−8 High, no referral lists or workflows), LinkedIn integration signals (−3 Medium, no LinkedIn Sales Navigator indicators). A systematic referral program is a meaningful retention multiplier for security services businesses with high trust requirements.

CONVERT.heading: Re-engage warm/missed opportunities
CONVERT.summary: Score: 41 (Poor). The limiting tier. Five structural gaps including one auto-critical trigger.

paragraphs.body: The Sales Blitz playbook identifies 17 required lists for systematic CONVERT execution. 11 of these are missing from your portal: Past Meetings - No Deal; Lost Deals segmentation; MQLs; SQLs; Form Submissions 30/60/90; Open Deals active-review; No-follow-up 30/60/90; Website visitor leads; Follow-up tasks view; No-shows; Trade show attendees. The auto-critical trigger is the missing Leads-not-contacted-in-30/60/90 list. Your stalled-deal list is present (your pipeline has an explicit Stalled Deal stage), so deal velocity is partially trackable — but without the leads-not-contacted list, top-of-funnel attrition is invisible.
Three workflow gaps identified: MQL-to-SQL handoff automation, lead reassignment on no-response, stalled deal alert. Each of these is a −8 High deduction.

In Quantum's experience auditing more than 55 HubSpot portals, the CONVERT tier is consistently where the most revenue leaks occur. Every opportunity already paid for through marketing spend, events, or prior sales effort sits in the CONVERT tier. A portal that executes CONVERT well recovers significantly more of its own CAC; a portal that does not execute CONVERT well pays for the same leads twice.

EXPAND.heading: Net-new clients
EXPAND.summary: Score: 81 (Good). Three structural gaps, none critical.

paragraphs.body: Gaps identified: ICP property exists but 0% fill rate on active customers (−8 High), Target Accounts property exists but 0 companies flagged (−8 High), no ZoomInfo intent or scoops signals in lists or workflows (−3 Medium). Your strategic infrastructure is present; it just isn't populated. Populating ICP on your top 100 active customers alone would close this gap.
